lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Here's a small idea that saves hours: write your résumé once, and get a web page, a PDF and data for your own site, all from the same file.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: It's called JSON Resume, an open, community-maintained format. You keep a single file named resume dot JSON, and themes handle the look. Names like Elegant, Paper, Kendall and Flat all read the same data.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: So it's like separating the content from the costume.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: That's the idea. And the file is organized in predictable blocks. Basics holds your name, headline, email and profiles. Work lists roles with company, title, dates and a short summary. Then education, skills with keywords, and projects with a link.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: How do you turn it into something people can read?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Install the command-line tool with npm, write the file against the schema, pick a theme, and run resume export. Give it a name ending in H T M L or P D F, and you have either one. You can also publish to the free JSON Resume registry for a hosted page.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: What if you run a Hugo site?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: There's a Hugo module that maps those same sections into templates, even in several languages. So the same data becomes a C V section inside a personal blog.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Several. Profile Studio gives a live preview as you edit. SkillSet draws your skills with D3. And there's a tool that starts your file from an existing LinkedIn profile.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: A developer C V that changes often is a strong fit. For ATS portals, the same data helps you generate plain text to paste.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: One source of truth, themes for layout, and the same file working in a command line or in Hugo. The full post has sample themes and code for each section.
